1 دَحَرَهُ , (S, A, K,) aor.
دَحَرَ , (K,) inf. n. دُحُورٌ (S, A, K) and دَحْرٌ, (T, K,) He (God, S) drove him away; expelled, or banished, him: he removed him; put, or placed, him at a distance, or away, or far away: (T, S, A, K:) he pushed, thrust, or repelled, him, (K,) with roughness, or violence, and ignominy. (TA.) It is said, in a form of prayer, اَلّٰهُمَّ ٱدْحَرْ عَنَّا الشَّيْطَانَ O God, drive away from us the devil. (TA.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
